hero.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.subheading: Everything you need to know about your professional culinary journey at CIB.

faqs.question: Will I really get an international job after this course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. Most Bangladeshis abroad end up in low-wage labor because they lack technical skills. Our [culinary course in Bangladesh](/culinary-course-bangladesh) teaches 120+ recipes with NSDA (Prime Minister's Office) accreditation, qualifying you for professional chef positions in global 5-star hospitality markets.
faqs.fullAnswer: Absolutely. Most people who go abroad end up in odd jobs or dishwashing because they lack technical skills and certification. In our course, you will master 120+ authentic recipes from 16+ countries. With this professional knowledge and NSDA accreditation, you gain the ability to join 5-star hotels globally as a professional chef. Stop trading time for low wages; earn your worth.

faqs.question: Is the certificate valid internationally?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. Our NSDA (National Skill Development Authority, Prime Minister's Office) Level-2 & 3 certification is a government-verified credential recognized globally. It serves as institutional proof of your culinary expertise for professional chef positions.
faqs.fullAnswer: Yes, our certifications are designed for global recognition. Being an NSDA approved Skill Training Provider (STP) under the Prime Minister's Office ensures your credentials carry significant weight internationally. Whether you are applying for a job in the Middle East, Europe, or beyond, your CIB and NSDA certificates prove you have mastered professional-grade culinary operations.

faqs.question: Does CIB guarantee a job or visa?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB is a training institute, not a recruitment agency. We provide the high-end skills and certificates required for global careers. We connect top performers with partner agencies for abroad guidance, but we do not guarantee visas or jobs.
faqs.fullAnswer: Honesty is our policy. CIB is a vocational powerhouse dedicated to training. We do not provide job guarantees or visa processing services. However, we have a vast network of hiring partners and agencies. Top performers may receive conditional placement support or guidance for international career paths based on their practical performance.

faqs.question: Will you help me find job after the course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes, CIB provides robust career support. While we don't guarantee jobs, our dedicated placement cell actively connects top-performing graduates with our network of 5-star hotels, premium restaurants, and international recruitment agencies for interviews and internship opportunities.
faqs.fullAnswer: Yes, career advancement is our primary objective. While no ethical institute can 'guarantee' a job, CIB provides robust, proactive career support. We maintain a dedicated placement cell that bridges the gap between our graduates and the hospitality industry. We actively leverage our deep industry network to connect top-performing, highly disciplined students directly with HR departments at 5-star hotels, premium restaurant groups, and verified international recruitment agencies. We arrange campus interviews, facilitate internships, and provide CV building and interview preparation workshops to ensure you are fully equipped to secure premium culinary positions.

faqs.question: What if I don't have prior cooking experience?
faqs.seoAnswer: No prior experience is required. Our course starts from the absolute basics—knife handling and basic cuts—before progressing to complex global cuisines like Pizza, Burger, and Fine Dining Plating. We build your skills from the ground up.
faqs.fullAnswer: You don't need to know how to cook to join us. We assume zero prior knowledge. We start with the art of using a knife and progress through 120+ international dishes. Whether you are a student, a career shifter, or an entrepreneur, we build your skills from the ground up. By the end of the program, your comprehensive training will surpass that of many individuals who have spent years learning informally.

faqs.question: Can I get a chef job abroad after completing a course in Bangladesh?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. CIB graduates receive international placements and credit transfer pathways to top universities. For details on enrollment requirements, check our [culinary course in Bangladesh](/culinary-course-bangladesh) curriculum.
faqs.fullAnswer: Yes, absolutely. CIB graduates receive robust international placements and credit transfer pathways to top universities in Malaysia, Australia, and Canada, backed by prestigious five-star hotel internships. CIB's comprehensive curriculum is globally recognized and fully aligned with international hospitality standards, allowing our students to secure high-paying chef positions in top-tier cruise lines, luxury resort properties, and fine-dining establishments across the globe upon graduation.

faqs.question: Can I miss a class? Do you have make-up sessions?

With CIB certification and international placement, salaries in Gulf countries range from 65,000-95,000 BDT monthly, tax-free.

faqs.question: How can I get a chef job abroad from Bangladesh?
faqs.seoAnswer: Complete a professional chef course with international certifications (NSDA, ISO/HACCP). Build 1-2 years experience through internships at 3-5 star hotels. Prepare an English language test score (IELTS 5.5+). Apply through verified recruitment agencies for Gulf, European, or Australian positions. CIB provides conditional placement support and connects graduates with partner agencies.
faqs.fullAnswer: Securing a chef job abroad requires a strategic approach. First, complete a professional chef course from an accredited institute like CIB to obtain NSDA and ISO/HACCP certifications. Second, build 1-2 years of solid practical experience through internships or jobs at local 3-5 star hotels. Third, prepare your English language proficiency; an IELTS score of 5.5 or higher significantly boosts your chances for global markets. Once qualified, apply exclusively through verified, government-approved recruitment agencies targeting Gulf, European, or Australian positions. CIB actively supports its top graduates by providing conditional placement assistance and connecting them directly with our trusted partner agencies to ensure a safe and successful international career transition.

faqs.question: Is NSDA certification recognized abroad?
faqs.seoAnswer: The National Skill Development Authority (NSDA) operates under Bangladesh's Prime Minister's Office. Its certifications follow the National Technical Vocational Qualification Framework (NTVQF). While NSDA is a Bangladeshi national credential, it demonstrates standardized competency to employers in the Gulf and Middle East regions. Combined with ISO-HACCP, it builds a strong CV for international applications.
faqs.fullAnswer: The National Skill Development Authority (NSDA) is the highest skill regulatory body operating directly under the Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh. It follows the National Technical Vocational Qualification Framework (NTVQF), ensuring training meets rigorous international standards. While the NSDA certificate is technically a national credential, its strict assessment protocols are highly respected by employers in the Gulf and Middle East. When foreign recruiters see an NSDA Level-3 certification, they know the candidate has passed comprehensive practical and theoretical evaluations. When combined with our ISO 22000 and HACCP food safety certifications, your CV becomes highly competitive for international 5-star hotel applications.

faqs.question: Why is HACCP certification important for chefs?
faqs.seoAnswer: Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) is an internationally recognized food safety standard aligned with WHO and FAO guidelines. 5-star hotels in Dubai and Gulf countries require HACCP certification for kitchen staff. Without it, your CV will be rejected at the screening stage. With it, you are eligible for higher salary bands and senior kitchen positions.
faqs.fullAnswer: HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) is not just an optional certificate; it is the global baseline for food safety. It is an internationally recognized standard aligned with WHO and FAO guidelines that prevents biological, chemical, and physical hazards in food production environments. Every 5-star hotel, international cruise line, and premium restaurant in Dubai and across the Gulf legally requires HACCP certification for their kitchen staff. Without this credential, international recruiters will automatically reject your CV during the initial screening stage. By acquiring HACCP certification at CIB, you instantly bypass this barrier, becoming eligible for higher salary bands, senior kitchen positions, and faster visa processing for abroad opportunities.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to start a cloud kitchen in Bangladesh?

This covers basic kitchen equipment, initial ingredient stock, licensing (Trade License, BFSA clearance), basic branding, and registration with food delivery platforms like Foodpanda. CIB's curriculum includes menu engineering and food costing training to help you launch profitably.

This capital covers essential commercial kitchen equipment, initial ingredient inventory, mandatory licensing (including Trade License and Bangladesh Food Safety Authority clearance), basic digital branding, and onboarding fees for delivery platforms like Foodpanda and Pathao. The key to cloud kitchen survival is strict margin control. CIB's professional curriculum goes beyond recipes; we teach critical business skills including menu engineering, portion control, and precise food costing. This comprehensive training ensures you can price your items competitively while maintaining strong profitability from day one.

faqs.question: What licenses do I need to open a restaurant in Bangladesh?
faqs.seoAnswer: To operate a food business in Bangladesh, you need: Trade License from City Corporation, Food Safety License from BFSA (Bangladesh Food Safety Authority), Fire Safety Clearance, VAT Registration, TIN, and for food processing facilities, a Factory License from DIFE. CIB provides food safety (HACCP) certification that helps satisfy BFSA requirements. For a detailed guide on the application process, read our [step-by-step guide to food business licenses in Bangladesh](/blog/food-business-license-bangladesh-process).
faqs.fullAnswer: Opening a legitimate restaurant in Bangladesh requires navigating several regulatory frameworks. The foundational requirements include: a Trade License from the local City Corporation, a Food Safety License from the Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA), Fire Safety Clearance from the Fire Service and Civil Defense, VAT Registration (BIN), and a TIN certificate. If you are operating a larger food processing facility or bakery, you may also need a Factory License from DIFE. Securing the BFSA license requires demonstrating strict hygiene standards. CIB's comprehensive ISO and HACCP training directly supports your compliance efforts, providing the documentation and operational knowledge required to satisfy BFSA inspectors and run a legally bulletproof food operation.

faqs.question: How can a housewife start a home baking business in Dhaka?
faqs.seoAnswer: Start with CIB's professional baking and pastry training to master artisan techniques and food safety standards. Register your business with a Trade License (home-based category). Create social media presence on Facebook and Instagram. Join food delivery platforms. Begin with 2-3 signature items. Many CIB graduates now run successful home bakeries earning 30,000-50,000+ BDT monthly.
faqs.fullAnswer: The home baking sector in Dhaka is booming, and housewives are perfectly positioned to capitalize on it. The first step is professionalizing your skills through CIB's comprehensive baking and pastry training, where you master artisan techniques, precise measurements, and crucial food hygiene standards. Once trained, register your business legally with a home-based Trade License. Build a strong digital presence by showcasing high-quality photos of your products on Facebook and Instagram. Start small—focus on 2-3 signature items (like custom fondant cakes or artisan brownies) rather than a massive menu. Integrate with local food delivery groups. With consistent quality and the professional foundation gained at CIB, many of our female graduates successfully manage home bakeries generating 30,000 to over 50,000 BDT in monthly profit.

faqs.question: How much does a chef course in Dhanmondi cost?
faqs.seoAnswer: The total course fee for the Professional Chef Course at CIB in Dhanmondi, Dhaka is 44,000 BDT. This covers all commercial ingredients, lab fees, and a professional chef kit (branded uniform, chef knife, and cutting board). There are absolutely no hidden charges, and a 3-installment payment option is available.
faqs.fullAnswer: The Professional Chef Course at CIB costs 44,000 BDT total, with no hidden expenses. You can secure your admission with a first installment of 16,000 BDT, while the remaining 28,000 BDT can be paid in two equal monthly installments of 14,000 BDT each. Unlike ordinary cooking classes, we do not charge extra for ingredients or kitchen usage. The fee fully covers premium raw materials, institutional worksheets, and a professional chef kit containing a branded uniform, cutting board, and a professional chef knife.

faqs.question: Can I get admitted to a chef course if I don't know how to cook?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. You do not need any prior cooking experience to join the CIB Chef Course. Our professional training starts from the absolute basics, covering safe knife skills, standard culinary cuts, and basic kitchen safety. Our mentors then guide you step-by-step to master complex continental and Asian recipes.
faqs.fullAnswer: Absolutely! Most of our students enter the program with zero prior kitchen experience. Our step-by-step curriculum is designed to accommodate absolute beginners. In your first sessions, you will not be cooking complex dishes; instead, you will learn the correct posture, knife safety, classical French cuts, and food hygiene principles. Once the foundation is solid, our executive chef mentors will guide you hands-on through 120+ recipes. We build your confidence from the ground up.

faqs.question: Which is the best cooking school in Dhaka with a government certificate?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB (Culinary Institute of Bangladesh) in Dhanmondi is widely recognized as the premier cooking school in Dhaka offering government-verified certificates. CIB is an approved Skill Training Provider (STP) under the Prime Minister's Office National Skills Development Authority (NSDA). Graduates receive NSDA Level-2 & 3 and ISO-HACCP certifications.
faqs.fullAnswer: CIB is Dhaka's top culinary academy providing official government-registered certifications. As a registered Skill Training Provider (STP) under the National Skill Development Authority (NSDA) of the Prime Minister's Office, we prepare students for national assessments. Additionally, we provide globally recognized ISO 22000 and HACCP food safety certificates verified by SGS Switzerland standards. This combination of government and international credentials makes CIB the ideal choice for launching a global culinary career.

faqs.question: Can I really get a job abroad after completing a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. Skilled and certified chefs are in high demand globally. With CIB's NSDA and ISO-HACCP certifications, you are qualified for professional positions in 5-star hotels, luxury cruise ships, and restaurants worldwide. CIB's placement cell actively connects top performing graduates with international recruitment agencies.
faqs.fullAnswer: Yes, professional chefs have excellent career mobility abroad. While unskilled workers often face low wages, certified chefs with recognized credentials command premium salaries. CIB's curriculum is aligned with global hospitality standards. Our NSDA Level 2 & 3 certificates and international HACCP credentials are highly valued across the Middle East, Europe, UK, and Canada. We actively support our graduates through our placement network, connecting them with verified recruiters for international hotel placements.

faqs.question: What is the address of CIB cooking school in Dhanmondi, Dhaka?
faqs.seoAnswer: The CIB Dhanmondi campus is located at House-160, 1st Floor (Beside Longlife Hospital), Lake Circus, Kalabagan, Dhanmondi, Dhaka-1205. For admissions or inquiries, call our official hotline number: +8801338958997.
faqs.fullAnswer: Our state-of-the-art commercial training kitchen is located in a prime area of Dhanmondi, Dhaka. The exact address is House-160, 1st Floor (directly beside Longlife Hospital), Lake Circus, Kalabagan, Dhanmondi, Dhaka-1205. It is easily accessible from the Kalabagan Bus Stand on Mirpur Road, just a short walk or rickshaw ride into Lake Circus Road. You are welcome to visit our campus to see a live class. For directions or booking a visit, call +8801338958997.

faqs.question: Can girls enroll in the professional chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes, women are highly encouraged to enroll in the professional chef course at CIB. We maintain a secure, respectful, and professional co-educational training environment. Many of our female graduates are working in premium 5-star hotel kitchens or running successful home bakery and catering businesses in Dhaka.
faqs.fullAnswer: Absolutely! Women play a vital role in the hospitality industry, and our courses are designed to help them succeed. CIB Dhanmondi provides a safe, highly professional co-educational kitchen environment where all students are trained to 5-star standards. Our instructors offer personalized mentorship to build commercial kitchen stamina and technical skills. Many of our female alumni are currently working as professional chefs in major hotel chains or operating lucrative home-based food businesses and cloud kitchens.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS to get a chef job abroad?
faqs.seoAnswer: IELTS is not mandatory for all countries. You can work in Gulf countries (such as Dubai, Qatar, Saudi Arabia) without an IELTS score by passing practical kitchen and basic English interviews. However, Western countries like the UK, Canada, and Australia require a minimum IELTS score of 5.5 to 6.0 for skilled worker sponsorship visas.
faqs.fullAnswer: English language requirements depend entirely on your destination country. For Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations, hiring is based primarily on practical trade tests and conversational English interviews, meaning IELTS is not required. However, if your goal is skilled immigration or a sponsored work visa in the UK, Australia, or Canada, you must prove English proficiency, typically requiring an IELTS academic/general score between 5.5 and 6.0. Our Principal Dewan Ismail (IELTS 7.5) provides guidance to help students navigate these requirements.

faqs.question: How do I start a home baking cake business after learning baking?
faqs.seoAnswer: To start a home baking business, first complete CIB's professional baking course to master portion control, recipe consistency, and food hygiene. Set up an attractive social media page on Facebook and Instagram, apply for a home-based Trade License, and register with local delivery networks.
faqs.fullAnswer: Launching a successful home bakery requires consistent quality and strict food costing. CIB's professional baking and pastry course teaches you how to design custom cakes, control portions, and minimize ingredient waste. After completing your training, take professional photos of your creations and share them on Facebook and Instagram to attract local clients. Secure a home-based trade license for legitimacy, and partner with local delivery services to deliver custom cakes to your clients. This is a high-margin business with massive local demand.

faqs.question: What is the rule for paying chef course fees in installments?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB offers a flexible 3-installment payment plan to ease the financial commitment. You pay 16,000 BDT upon admission to secure your seat. The remaining balance of 28,000 BDT is paid in two equal monthly installments of 14,000 BDT each during the course. Payments are accepted via cash, mobile banking, or bank transfer.
faqs.fullAnswer: We believe financial constraints should not prevent passionate individuals from getting high-quality technical education. Our total course fee is 44,000 BDT, divided into three manageable stages. You pay an initial 16,000 BDT at the time of enrollment to book your slot. The second installment of 14,000 BDT is due at the end of the first month of classes, and the final 14,000 BDT is due at the end of the second month. You can complete payments via cash at our campus, mobile services (bKash/Nagad), or direct bank deposit.

faqs.question: How many months does a chef course take and how many class days per week?
faqs.seoAnswer: The Professional Chef Course at CIB is a 6-month program: 2 months of intensive practical lab classes (held 3 days a week, 3 hours per class) followed by a 4-month professional internship in a 5-star hotel. We offer morning, afternoon, and weekend batches to suit your schedule.
faqs.fullAnswer: The complete program takes 6 months. The initial 2 months consist of rigorous hands-on practical training in our commercial kitchen in Dhanmondi. Classes are held 3 days a week, with each session lasting 3 hours. Following the practical training, we place students in a 4-month internship at leading 5-star hotels. For university students or full-time employees, we offer a weekend batch (Friday & Saturday sessions) that covers the exact same curriculum and recipes without interfering with weekday schedules.

faqs.question: What kind of job can I get after completing a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: After completing a chef course, you can secure positions like Commis Chef, Pastry Chef, or Demi Chef in 5-star hotels, luxury resorts, cruise lines, and premium restaurants. With 2-3 years of experience, you can promote to Chef de Partie or Sous Chef. You can also start a cloud kitchen or home bakery.
faqs.fullAnswer: Completing a professional culinary program unlocks vast employment opportunities in the global hospitality sector. In Bangladesh, graduates can apply for internships and full-time chef positions at leading 5-star hotel conglomerates such as Renaissance Dhaka, The Westin, Radisson Blu, and Pan Pacific Sonargaon. Typically, fresh graduates enter the kitchen hierarchy as Commis-III or Assistant Chefs, focusing on basic preparations and station mis-en-place. Over the next few years, based on culinary consistency, speed, and discipline, you can advance to Demi-CDP, Chef de Partie (CDP), and eventually Sous Chef or Executive Chef. Internationally, there is a massive shortage of certified chefs, particularly in the GCC region (Dubai, Riyadh, Doha) and European luxury hospitality networks, offering highly paid tax-free contracts with accommodation. Alternatively, graduates can leverage their costing and menu planning knowledge to launch successful food trucks, cafes, or home bakeries.

faqs.question: How much does a chef course cost in Dhaka?
faqs.seoAnswer: The total course fee for the Professional Chef Course at CIB in Dhaka is 44,000 BDT. This covers all commercial ingredients, lab fees, study materials, and a professional chef kit (branded uniform, chef knife, and cutting board). A 3-installment option is available with no hidden charges.
faqs.fullAnswer: The cost of professional culinary education in Dhaka varies, but CIB Dhanmondi offers a premium, comprehensive 6-month Professional Chef Course for a total fee of 44,000 BDT. To make professional training accessible, we provide a flexible 3-stage installment plan. You pay an initial 16,000 BDT at enrollment to secure your seat. The remaining 28,000 BDT is split into two equal monthly installments of 14,000 BDT due at the end of the first and second months. Unlike many local culinary schools that charge separate fees for raw ingredients or exam sessions, CIB has a strict policy of zero hidden charges. The 44,000 BDT fee covers all premium ingredients (including salmon, imported cheese, and specialized herbs), your NSDA registration and assessment fees, and a professional chef kit consisting of a custom branded uniform, commercial cutting board, and a professional chef knife set.

faqs.question: Which chef course is best for women?
faqs.seoAnswer: For women, CIB's 6-month Professional Chef Course and our short Baking & Pastry Arts course are highly recommended. We offer a safe, respectful, and CCTV-monitored co-educational environment. These courses prepare women for careers in commercial kitchens or to run home bakeries.
faqs.fullAnswer: Culinary arts has become a highly lucrative and empowering career path for women. At CIB, the 6-month Professional Chef Course and the specialized Baking & Pastry Arts Course are particularly popular among female students. CIB Dhanmondi prioritizes a safe, respectful, and modern co-educational learning environment. Our kitchen labs are fully CCTV-monitored, and we enforce a strict corporate code of conduct with zero tolerance for harassment. The hands-on nature of the training builds commercial kitchen stamina, preparing women to manage high-pressure hot kitchen stations or work in luxury hotels. For those seeking home-based financial independence, our baking course provides detailed training in recipe scaling, food hygiene, costing, and advanced cake decoration, allowing housewives to launch profitable custom cake shops or catering brands from their own kitchens with active CIB marketing guidance.

faqs.question: How can I go abroad after doing a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Complete an NSDA-accredited chef course to secure government and ISO-HACCP certifications. Build 1-2 years of working experience in local 3-5 star hotels. Clear basic English language requirements (or IELTS 5.5+ for Western countries) and apply through verified BMET-approved recruitment agencies.
faqs.fullAnswer: Securing employment abroad as a professional chef involves a structured, legally compliant path. First, acquire government-recognized vocational credentials, such as the NSDA Level-2 or 3 certificate, alongside international food safety credentials (ISO 22000 and HACCP) from CIB. Second, you must gain 1 to 2 years of practical, hands-on experience in a local 3 to 5-star hotel kitchen to build your speed and recipe consistency. Third, language proficiency is vital: while GCC countries only require conversational English, Western markets like the UK, Australia, and Canada require a minimum IELTS score of 5.5 or language certification (e.g., German A2/B1 for Germany's Skilled Worker visa). Finally, register on the Ami Probashi portal and apply through BMET-approved recruitment agencies. CIB's dedicated career placement cell actively guides graduates with CV writing, video cooking portfolio creation, and trade test preparation to ensure success.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build a career as a chef?
faqs.seoAnswer: The foundational training takes 6 months (2 months of intensive practical kitchen lab classes + 4 months of 5-star hotel internship). However, establishing a strong career, mastering multiple kitchen sections, and promoting to senior roles like Chef de Partie or Sous Chef takes 3 to 5 years.
faqs.fullAnswer: Building a reputable culinary career is a progressive journey of skill acquisition. At CIB, your foundational journey takes 6 months: 2 months of intensive hands-on training in our commercial kitchen lab (held 3 days a week, 3 hours a day) followed by a 4-month on-the-job internship at a partner 5-star hotel. This 6-month phase qualifies you to start working as a Commis Chef. Transitioning from an entry-level cook to a competent Chef de Partie (CDP) who runs an entire station (like pastry, hot line, or cold larder) typically requires 3 to 4 years of active industry experience. Reaching the status of a Sous Chef or Executive Chef who manages budgets, menu engineering, and entire kitchen teams generally takes 5 to 8 years. Your growth speed is entirely determined by your discipline, culinary creativity, and continuous learning.

faqs.question: What are the working hours of a chef?
faqs.seoAnswer: Professional chefs work in shifts, typically averaging 8 to 10 hours a day. Because hotels and restaurants operate 24/7, chefs rotate between morning, afternoon, and night shifts. Busy holiday seasons require extra dedication, which is rewarded with service charge bonuses.
faqs.fullAnswer: A chef's working schedule is dynamic and shift-based, reflecting the 24/7 operating nature of the hospitality sector. Standard shifts average 8 to 10 hours daily, and chefs rotate between morning shifts (typically 6:00 AM to 3:00 PM), afternoon/dinner shifts (2:00 PM to 11:00 PM), and occasional night or overnight prep shifts. The weekly off-day is rotating and may fall on a weekday. Holiday seasons, Ramadan, and large banqueting events represent high-pressure periods that demand longer hours, though they are compensated with overtime pay and higher service charge distributions. The environment is highly structured, requiring military-like coordination and rapid execution. CIB simulates this shift-work environment during intensive practical sessions to help students adapt to the physical demands of commercial kitchens.

faqs.question: What documents are required for admission to a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: To enroll in a chef course at CIB, you need to submit copies of your educational certificates (SSC/HSC or equivalent), national identity card (NID) or digital birth registration, and 2 passport-sized color photos. No prior cooking experience or certificates are required.
faqs.fullAnswer: Admissions at the Culinary Institute of Bangladesh (CIB) follow a streamlined vocational enrollment process. To apply for our Professional Chef Course or any short-term specialty program, prospective students must submit: 1. A photocopy of their minimum SSC/HSC passing certificate or transcript (or any equivalent academic credential from any board). 2. A photocopy of their National Identity Card (NID) or digital Birth Registration Certificate. 3. Two recent passport-size color photographs. We do not require any past culinary experience, portfolios, or cooking certificates, as our training is designed to build skills from the ground up. Students from all streams (Science, Arts, Commerce, or Madrasah) are eligible. You can complete the process by visiting our Dhanmondi campus or submitting files online via our official portal.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a certificate after chef training?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB's institutional completion certificate and transcript are issued within 7 to 10 days after your practical exam. However, the government-registered NSDA Level certificate takes 1 to 2 months from the assessment date due to national processing and board approvals.
faqs.fullAnswer: Receiving your professional certifications is a multi-step verification process. Immediately after completing your 2-month intensive kitchen lab and passing the practical examination, CIB issues your Institutional Certificate and Grade Sheet within 7 to 10 working days. Upon finishing your 4-month 5-star hotel internship, you will receive an official internship experience certificate directly from the hotel's HR department. For the government NSDA Level certification, students undergo a practical assessment evaluated by external government assessors at our campus. The processing, verification, and official print of these digital and physical NSDA certificates by the Prime Minister's Office board typically take 1 to 2 months. This government certificate is registered online, making it highly valuable for visa and immigration verification.

faqs.question: Can a chef course be done online?
faqs.seoAnswer: A professional chef course cannot be completed entirely online because culinary arts is a practical, physical discipline. You must practice knife handling, temperature management, and flavor profile tuning in a commercial kitchen under the direct guidance of master chefs.
faqs.fullAnswer: While online cooking videos are useful for theoretical ideas, professional gastronomy requires physical, hands-on training that cannot be replicated through a screen. Crucial skills like safe knife control, precise vegetable cuts, tempura frying, baking dough consistency, and commercial oven safety must be practiced in a physical lab. CIB Dhanmondi provides every student with their own commercial workstation, allowing them to cook each recipe individually rather than in groups. This ensures you master the physical muscle memory required in a real kitchen. However, CIB does utilize hybrid models for our theoretical classes—such as food safety regulations (HACCP), menu design, food costing formulas, and hospitality English—which can be completed online for student convenience.

faqs.question: Is accommodation available for students coming from outside Dhaka for a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB does not operate its own hostels, but we provide full administrative support to students coming from outside Dhaka to help them find safe, affordable student housing, paying guest rooms, or shared messes near our Dhanmondi campus.
faqs.fullAnswer: We welcome students from all divisions of Bangladesh at CIB. While we do not have our own residential dormitories, our student welfare wing provides complete assistance in securing safe, clean, and affordable accommodation near the Dhanmondi and Kalabagan areas. There are numerous private student hostels, shared mess flats, and paying guest facilities within walking distance of our campus, with monthly rentals ranging from 3,000 to 6,000 BDT including basic meals. Our team provides verified contact details and pricing guides to make the transition smooth and safe for out-of-town students. Since classes are scheduled 3 days a week, many students successfully manage their schedules while living temporarily in Dhaka.

faqs.question: What salary can be expected after a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: In Bangladesh, entry-level Commis Chefs start at 15,000-25,000 BDT plus service charge distributions. Experienced Chef de Parties earn 35,000-60,000 BDT, while international placements in GCC countries offer tax-free salaries ranging from 65,000 to 95,000 BDT monthly.
faqs.fullAnswer: Culinary compensation is directly linked to experience, certification, and specialization. In Bangladesh's 5-star hotel sector, a fresh graduate starts as a Commis-III with a base salary of 15,000 to 25,000 BDT. However, they also receive monthly service charge distributions, which can double their take-home pay. With 3-5 years of experience, a Chef de Partie (CDP) earns 35,000 to 60,000 BDT. Internationally, particularly in GCC countries (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar), entry-level certified chefs receive tax-free salaries of 65,000 to 95,000 BDT, with employers covering visa, flights, health insurance, meals, and accommodation. Executive Chefs in Bangladesh's top hotels earn between 1,50,000 and 4,50,000 BDT monthly. CIB's premium training is designed to fast-track your path to these high-earning salary brackets.

faqs.question: At what age should one start a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: The ideal age to start a chef course is between 16 and 35, as this period offers the best physical stamina and learning speed for commercial kitchens. However, there is no upper age limit, and CIB has successfully trained many students aged 40+.
faqs.fullAnswer: There is no strict age limit to pursue culinary arts, though the most common age bracket for starting a professional chef career is 16 to 35. This age range is ideal due to the physical nature of commercial kitchen work, which involves standing for long shifts and handling heavy equipment. Younger students also adapt quickly to knife skills, culinary English, and kitchen discipline. However, cooking is a lifelong passion. CIB regularly trains students in their 40s and 50s—including career switchers, retirees, and homemakers—who successfully complete our baking or cooking courses and go on to establish highly profitable home bakeries, catering companies, or restaurants. If you possess passion, discipline, and a willingness to learn, age is not a barrier.

faqs.question: Is it essential to know English to become a chef?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes, basic English is highly important. Commercial kitchens use English for recipe manuals, ingredients labeling, and classical French culinary terms. Furthermore, clearing basic English communication is essential for passing international job interviews and visa processing.
faqs.fullAnswer: While you don't need to be an expert in English literature, a basic working knowledge of English is essential for modern culinary success. Commercial kitchens globally operate in English. All standard recipe manuals, international menu items, safety labels, and classical French culinary terms (like julienne, chiffonade, mirepoix, or sauté) are written in English. Communication with international hotel guests, suppliers, and foreign Executive Chefs also requires basic English. For those aiming for skilled work visas in the UK, Canada, or Australia, passing an English proficiency test (like IELTS with a minimum 5.5 score) is mandatory. CIB provides bilingual instruction: we explain concepts in Bengali but enforce the use of correct culinary English terms to prepare you for global roles.

faqs.question: How are the classes conducted in a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: CIB classes are highly structured and hands-on. Each 3-hour session begins with a brief theoretical review of the recipe and a live culinary demonstration by the mentor chef. Students then spend the remaining 2 hours cooking the dish individually at their own workstations.
faqs.fullAnswer: Classes at CIB are structured according to international vocational training standards. Each class is 3 hours long. The first 30 minutes consist of a briefing where the mentor chef explains the recipe's ingredients, culinary history, food science, and specific safety points. The next 30 minutes feature a live demonstration: the master chef cooks the dish, demonstrating proper knife cuts, cooking temperatures, and plating aesthetics. The final 2 hours are dedicated to student practice. Each student is assigned a commercial workstation with their own burner, oven, and raw ingredients. You cook the entire recipe individually, under the close supervision of our instructors. At the end of the class, the chef tastes and evaluates your dish on flavor balance, texture, and presentation, providing constructive feedback.

faqs.question: Can the chef course fee be paid in installments?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. CIB offers a flexible 3-installment payment plan for the 44,000 BDT Professional Chef Course. You pay 16,000 BDT at admission to secure your seat, followed by two monthly installments of 14,000 BDT each. We accept cash, card, and mobile banking.
faqs.fullAnswer: We believe financial constraints should never prevent a talented student from acquiring high-value technical skills. To support our students, CIB offers a flexible 3-part installment plan for the 44,000 BDT Professional Chef Course, with no hidden interest or admin fees. You pay 16,000 BDT upon admission to confirm your slot and receive your chef kit. The second installment of 14,000 BDT is due at the end of the first month of classes, and the final 14,000 BDT is due at the end of the second month. We accept cash at our campus office, direct bank deposits, and mobile financial services (bKash, Nagad, Rocket) for easy remote payments, ensuring you can focus on mastering your culinary skills without financial stress.

faqs.question: How is the practical training in a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Over 95% of our curriculum is practical. CIB students train in state-of-the-art commercial kitchen labs, handling real premium ingredients (like fresh salmon, chicken, herbs, and sauces) individually. We do not use group cooking, ensuring every student masters the recipe.
faqs.fullAnswer: Culinary arts is a craft learned through practice, not reading. Over 95% of CIB's curriculum is hands-on. Our training labs are modeled after 5-star commercial hotel kitchens, equipped with commercial ranges, prep tables, and professional ovens. In every class, you are provided with your own portion of fresh ingredients—such as beef, salmon, seafood, cheese, and fresh herbs. Unlike other centers where students cook in groups, CIB requires every student to cook their own dish from start to finish. This builds the muscle memory and speed required in commercial operations. Our experienced instructors stand by your side to correct your knife angles, cooking temperatures, and plating techniques in real time.

faqs.question: Can I start a restaurant business after doing a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. A chef course is the perfect foundation for opening a restaurant, cafe, or cloud kitchen. Besides cooking, CIB teaches critical business skills like portion control, food costing formulas, menu engineering, and kitchen design to prevent financial loss.
faqs.fullAnswer: Opening a food business is a lucrative venture if managed correctly. CIB's Professional Chef Course goes beyond teaching recipes; we prepare you for entrepreneurship. We teach critical kitchen business modules, including food costing formulas, portion sizing, inventory management, and menu engineering. Understanding these concepts helps you control food wastage, which is the leading cause of restaurant failures. Knowing how to run a kitchen also reduces your reliance on hired Head Chefs, preventing operational disruptions. CIB has helped numerous alumni launch successful restaurants, cafes, and cloud kitchens in Dhaka. We provide guidance on trade licenses, food safety registrations (BFSA), and kitchen layouts.

faqs.question: What certificates are required to get a chef job abroad?
faqs.seoAnswer: To work abroad legally, you need an NSDA-accredited vocational certificate, a globally recognized ISO 22000 Food Safety Management certificate, and a HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) certificate. CIB's 6-month program includes all these mandatory credentials.
faqs.fullAnswer: International employers, particularly in Europe, UK, and the Middle East, legally require certified proof of skill and food safety compliance. The mandatory credentials include: 1. An accredited vocational certificate (such as the NSDA Level certificate from the Prime Minister's Office). 2. A HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) certificate, which proves you understand food safety hazard prevention. 3. An ISO 22000 Food Safety Management certificate. These certifications must be issued by or aligned with international auditing bodies like SGS Switzerland. Without these, your CV will be filtered out by HR systems. CIB's Professional Chef Course includes these certifications, validating your qualifications globally.

faqs.question: Is there job placement assistance after completing a chef course?
faqs.seoAnswer: Yes. CIB has a dedicated Career Placement Cell that arranges a 4-month internship at partner 5-star hotels for top performing students. We also support graduates with CV writing, video portfolio creation, and connections to verified international recruiting agencies.
faqs.fullAnswer: CIB is committed to your employment success. Our dedicated Career Placement Cell works closely with graduates. After completing the 2-month practical training, we arrange a 4-month internship at leading partner 5-star hotels (like Renaissance, Radisson, InterContinental) for qualified students. A successful internship often leads directly to full-time employment at the hotel. We also conduct workshops on CV preparation, teach interview skills, and help students record high-quality cooking videos for their portfolios. Additionally, we connect alumni with government-approved recruiting agencies for job opportunities in the Gulf and Europe.

faqs.question: Which subjects do I need to be good at to become a chef?
faqs.seoAnswer: You do not need to be an expert in any academic subject to become a chef. However, basic math is useful for recipe scaling and costing, basic English is important for international kitchens, and basic science helps you understand food chemistry. Passion and discipline are the most critical factors.
faqs.fullAnswer: Culinary arts is a practical combination of math, science, and creative art. You do not need an advanced academic degree, but basic skills in a few areas are helpful: 1. Basic Math: Necessary for scaling recipes (multiplying ingredients) and calculating food costing and portion sizes. 2. Basic English: Essential because international kitchen terms, recipe manuals, and equipment instructions are in English. 3. Basic Science: Helps you understand food chemistry, such as how heat changes proteins, how yeast works in bread, or how emulsions are formed in sauces. Above all, the most important requirements are physical stamina, discipline, attention to detail, and a passion for food. CIB's instructors will teach you all the necessary technical skills.

cta.heading: Ready to Apply?
cta.subtext: Secure your seat for the next batch. Enrollment is currently open.
